elements.element: Governing law is the law of the State of New York
elements.evidence: "governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York"

elements.element: Exclusive jurisdiction in the state courts in New York County
elements.evidence: "the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction"

elements.element: Exclusive jurisdiction in the federal courts in New York County
elements.evidence: "state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction"

elements.element: Law and forum form a permitted corresponding pair (NY law with NY County courts)
elements.evidence: § 28.1 now pairs "laws of the State of New York" with "courts located in New York County, New York"; the residual carve-out in § 28.2 is limited to "temporary injunctive relief" for confidentiality/IP and is pre-existing, untouched language

elements.element: Alternative: Delaware, California, or England and Wales law with correspondingly located courts
elements.evidence: Clause selects New York law and New York County courts, not any fallback pair

offending_extra_words: and the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction
reasons: Preferred level is complete: New York governing law with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County, a permitted corresponding pair.

Minimality fails: § 28.2 already vests exclusive jurisdiction in "The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York", so restating the same forum in § 28.1 duplicates existing protection. A tighter edit (swapping the law reference and deleting the Singapore forum wording, leaving § 28.2 to supply the forum) would have sufficed; the operation expands 13 words to 27.

Intent is preserved: the injunctive-relief carve-out, personal-jurisdiction submission and venue waiver in § 28.2 remain effective and no undefined term or contradiction is introduced (the prior Singapore/New York conflict is resolved).
Fallback is not engaged; the drafter's locked target (preferred) is the operative bargain and no fallback element is borrowed.
